minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JULY 11, 2023

  CALL TO ORDER  Maria del Pilar Avalos, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to
  order to 6:31 p.m.

  INVOCATION  Steve Costley, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation

  PLEDGE OF
  ALLEGIANCE  Darren Arakawa, Police Chief

  ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

  PRESENT  Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Vice Mayor Gil Hurtado, Council Member
  Joshua Barron, Council Member Maria Davila, and Council Member Al
  Rios; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Chris Jeffers, City
  Attorney Raul F. Salinas

  1
  LAW ENFORCEMENT  Following the conclusion of a public hearing, the City Council
  unanimously accepted and appropriated the FY 2022/23 Edward Byrne
11.......
  Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Funds, in the amount of $48,387 for
  the purchase of equipment for sworn personnel by motion of Council
  Member Davila and seconded by Mayor Avalos.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Barron, yes; Council Member Davila,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Mayor Avalos,
  yes.

  Darren Arakawa, Police Chief, explains the proposed use of the funding
  this year will be to offset the cost for the Acts On program and to continue
  the use of necessary equipment out of the field.

  Resident Mario Dominguez states his support for the funding and asked
  about the camera usage on Police officers.

  Mr. Arakawa explained that every Officer on the field has been assigned a
  camera and the policy is that anytime an Officer has any contact with the
  community the body camera is activated.

  COMMENTS FROM THE
  AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
..•.  ITEMS)  Resident Gabriel Torres expressed how much he enjoys working in the
  park and wanted to propose the idea of having an event called "Car free
  Sunday" on the Tweedy Mile. It would consist of the community coming
  together and allowing vendors to sell.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE (NON-AGENDA
ITEMS) CONT'D  Resident Mario Dominguez commented with his support on the "Car Free
  Sunday" idea and then expressed frustration over false accusations
  regarding the council members.

  Resident Thomas Buckley asked about an update on an upcoming deficit.

  Liz Ruiz, Resident on Kauffman St, asked for an update on the
  construction of the entrance of the 710 Fwy on Firestone and also an
  upcoming meeting at the Parks and Recreation Department.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, provided the information that
  there are updates of the 710 Fwy construction on the city's website and
  they are scheduled to complete design in March of 2024.

  Kristopher Ryan, Director of Administrative Services, addressed the issue
  on the deficit of the general fund and stated that the public has access to
  the general budget forecast online on the city's website.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Steve Costley, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation, announced the
  annual Fun Run at South Gate Park and the Art Festival on the river.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development, stated the
  extension of the Home Recognition program to August 31st and highly
  encourages everyone to participate.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, announced new positions
  that are listed on the city's website.

  Darren Arakawa, Police Chief publicly recognized Officer Georgina
  Vargas for aggressively pursuing drunk drivers in the city of South Gate.
  He also announced that they have received a grant award from the Alcohol
  and Beverage Control for their enforcement efforts.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager, reported that State Senator Gonzalez and
  Assembly Member Rendon were able to secure 2.7 million dollars to
  apply for capital projects. He also stated the EPA meeting that will take
  place at South Gate Park concerning properties that are contaminated
  (5211 Southern Ave. and 9301 Rayo Ave). The allegations against the
  council were addressed as well.

  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney, spoke on the allegations and criticism
  against the council.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, encourages everyone to participate in the Fun
  Run at South Gate Park.
  Page 2 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

Am.  REPORTS AND COMMENTS
  FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  CONT'D  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, commended the LA County Police
  Department and Fire Department for their quick response in aiding a
  bicyclist along the LA River that suffered a cardiac arrest.

  Council Member Barron described his experience in public events he
  attended in the city. He also encouraged residents to participate in the
  Home Recognition program and there are still open slots for the swim
  lessons.

  Council Member Davila expressed thoughts on the Car Free Sunday
  proposal and believes it is a good idea. She also thanked the Police
  Department for their efforts.

  Council Member Rios expressed how interested he is in upcoming
  activities and proposed activities.

  Vice Mayor Hurtado states a need to publicize the Backpack giveaway to
  be able to reach all families that need the supplies. He also expressed his
  thoughts on comments from Mr. Dominguez on the allegations of the
  council.

  Mayor Avalos commended Gabriel Torres on his engagement for the city
  of South Gate and the Police Officers who protected City Hall during
  council meetings.

  Mario Dominguez wanted any updates regarding the camera system in the
  Council Chambers.

  Thomas Buckley wanted to thank the community and express
  disappointment with the council for not allowing more callers speak
  during the prior meeting.

  Mr. Jeffers touched base on the camera system requested by Mr.
  Dominguez and stated the process needed to move forward.

  CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 were approved by motion of
  Council Member Davila and seconded by Council Member Rios.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Barron, yes (recused on Item 6); Council
  Member Davila, yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes
  (recused on Item 3); Mayor Avalos, yes (recused on Item 6).

  Page 3 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

2
MUNICIPAL CODE
ADMIN  The City Council unanimously waived the reading in full and adopted
  Ordinance No. 2023-04-CC entitled Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of South Gate, California, amending provisions of the South Gate
  Municipal Code pertaining to Sidewalk Vendors Section 2.10.150
  (Businesses requiring a business permit) and Section 2.10.970 (Sidewalk
  Vending Program) of Chapter 2.10 (Business Regulation) of Title 2
  (Licenses - Business Regulations), and Section 7.39.010 (Sales from
  Nonmotorized Vehicles on City Streets Prohibited) of Chapter 7.39 (Sales
  from Nonmotorized Vehicles on City Streets Prohibited Except During
  City-Sponsored Parades) of Title 7 (Public Safety And Morals), and
  Section 8.14.010 (Unlawful Parking - Peddlers, Vendors and Vehicles
  advertised for sale or rent) of Chapter 8.14 (Unlawful Parking - Peddlers,
  Vendors and Vehicles Advertised for Sale or Rent) of Title 8 (Traffic) of
  the South Gate Municipal Code during Consent Calendar.

3
STREETS/SIDEWALKS/
LANDSCAPING  The City Council made a finding and adopted Resolution No. 2023-44-
  CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate, State
  of California, declaring an emergency still exists and authorizing repair,
  replacement or maintenance activities of public facilities related to the
  Urban Orchard, City Project No. 539-PRK, without public bidding,
  pursuant to the emergency contracting procedures of the South Gate
  Municipal Code and the California Public Contract Code during Consent
  Calendar.

4
PERSONNEL BENEFITS/
RETIREMENT ADMIN  The City Council unanimously adopted Resolution No. 2023-45-
  CC entitled Resolution of the City Council of the City of South Gate,
  California, approving the initiation of the Ca1PERS process for retirement
  cost sharing under Government Code Section 20516(a) for unclassified
  executive management contract employees during Consent Calendar.

5
ANIMAL CONTROL  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  Amendment No. 4 to Contract No. 3525 with the Southeast
  Area Animal Control Authority for annual cost increase for animal
  control and sheltering services in an amount not to exceed
  $792,630 for Fiscal Year 2023/24; and

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Page 4 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

6
TRANSPORTATION
PLANNING/ADMIN  The City Council approved items A & B during Consent Calendar.

  a.  Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. 3378 Measure R Funding
  Agreement with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan
  Transportation Authority ("Metro") retroactively extending the
  lapsing date from June 30, 2022 to June 30, 2024, for the Firestone
  Boulevard Regional Corridor Capacity Enhancement Phase II
  Project, City Project No. 476-TRF Metro Project ID No.
  MR306.33; and

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 3 in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

7
PUBLIC WORKS/
ENGINEERING ADMIN  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  Amendment No. 3 to Contract No. 2020-16-CC with KOA
  Corporation for a street lighting engineering study for an amount
  not to exceed $62,418; and

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreements in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Liz Ruiz wanted more clarification on the street light replacement project.

  Mr. Cervantez went into detail about the KOA amendment and the need for
  the project.

8
WATER  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B & C during Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  Agreement (Contract No. 2023-96-CC) with HydroScientific West
  to upgrade the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System
  Upgrade, City Project No. 647-WTR, in an amount not to exceed
  $597,621;

  b.  Appropriated $200,000 in Water Funds from the unrestricted
  balance of the Water Fund to fully fund the project; and

  c.  Authorized the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  Page 5 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

9
DATA PROCESSING
SERVICES  The City Council unanimously approved items A & B during Consent
  Calendar.

  a.  Professional Services Agreement (Contract No. 2023-97-CC) with
  ClientFirst Technology Consulting for project management
  services associated with the City's Technology Master Plan in an
  amount not-to-exceed $150,000;

  b.  Authorized the Mayor to execute agreement in a form acceptable
  to the City Attorney.

10
MINUTES  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C, D & E during
  Consent Calendar.

  a.  The Regular Meeting minutes of February 14, 2023;

  b.  The Regular Meeting minutes of April 11, 2023;

  c.  The Regular Meeting minutes of May 23, 2023;

  d.  The Special and Regular Meeting minutes of June 13, 2023; and

  e.  The Special Meeting minutes of June 20, 2023.

11
WASTEWATER MGMT  The City Council unanimously approved items A, B, C & D by motion of
  Council Member Rios and seconded by Council Member Barron.

  a.  Receiving and filing the Sewer Rate Study Report;

  b.  Selecting Alternative No. 2 of the Sewer Rate Study for the
  proposed sewer rate structure changes and directing staff to initiate
  the Proposition 218 process;

  c.  Approving an Agreement (Contract No. 2023-98-CC) with NBS
  Financial Group (NBS) in an amount not to exceed $32,500 to
  conduct the required Proposition 218 process, including
  educational material development; and

  d.  Authorizing the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form
  acceptable to the City Attorney.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Barron, yes; Council Member Davila,
  yes; Council Member Rios, yes; Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Mayor Avalos,
  yes.

  Page 6 of 7
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JULY 11, 2023

12
WARRANTS  The City Council unanimously approved the Warrant Register for July 11,
  2023, by motion of Mayor Avalos and seconded by Vice Mayor Hurtado.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Barron, yes; Council Member Davila,
  yes, Council Member Rios, yes, Vice Mayor Hurtado, yes; Mayor Avalos,
  yes.

  Total of Checks:  $2,163,641.57
  Less: Voids  (55.00)
  Less: Employee Payroll Deductions  $ (372,705.82)
  Grand Total:  $1,790,880,75
